notes:
No code changed in this round: the three checklist areas I could close in code are already covered by tests at bdc5fb5, and the remaining gaps need the owner.
1. Requirement gate (owner): R42/R43 are not done until production code records into the log and sign-off calls require_intact. That is the case store (cases/<id>/log.jsonl, `cma case new|import`) and sign-off (T27). Adding a CLI caller in T12 would be designing C3/C6 here, so I did not. Either re-scope T12 to building-block acceptance or make T12 pass only together with the first caller task.
2. Observability/alerting: the design's signals (a structured event line per log entry, a refusal with a red banner and non-zero exit when the chain breaks, `cma report`) all live in callers that do not exist yet. Need a test at the caller asserting the non-zero exit on CaseLogBroken.
3. Performance: verify is O(n) and the head file stores every hash, so each append rewrites O(n) bytes (134 KB, ~30 ms at 2,000 entries). Fine for the expected case sizes; set a bound or a target if cases can reach tens of thousands of events.
4. A deleted head file beside a one-entry log, or one log line plus a deleted head, reads as a torn first append, not as tampering, so drop_torn_entry is allowed. Rewriting log and head file together is undetectable (documented); the sign-off must pin the head hash it saw (T27).
5. A reader without write permission on the case folder that meets a torn log raises PermissionError from opening the lock file, not CaseLogBroken. Low risk (one OS user owns the case root, R31), but a read-only consumer (verify, report) should catch it.
6. Docs: no changelog line; the format is documented only in the module docstring. Add a release-note line when the first command ships.
